title: SailPoint Admin Domain 2 questions (2.1, 2.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: What is the main reason an organization deploys a SailPoint virtual appliance (VA)?
choices: To connect the tenant securely to sources inside the organization's network
To store nightly backups of the tenant configuration
To replace identity profiles for on-premises users
To host a local copy of the tenant's identity database for faster user sign-in
questions.answer: To connect the tenant securely to sources inside the organization's network
questions.explanation: A VA is the bridge between the multi-tenant cloud service and systems the cloud cannot reach directly, such as on-premises directories and databases. It does not hold the tenant's identity data or configuration backups.

questions.stem: A firewall engineer asks which inbound connections from SailPoint's cloud must be opened to the VAs so aggregations can run. What should the administrator tell the engineer?
choices: Inbound 443 from SailPoint's published cloud addresses to every VA host
Inbound 8443 from the tenant's API gateway
None are needed, because each VA polls SailPoint over outbound HTTPS
Inbound 22 so the tenant can run remote commands
questions.answer: None are needed, because each VA polls SailPoint over outbound HTTPS
questions.explanation: VAs initiate all communication outbound on 443 and pull their work from the cluster's queue. Port 22 inbound is only for administrators on the internal network to sign in to the VA.

questions.stem: An administrator starts an account aggregation on an on-premises Active Directory source. How does that request reach a virtual appliance?
choices: The tenant opens an SSH session to a VA and starts the aggregation
The administrator's browser sends the request straight to the VA
The domain controllers push the accounts to the tenant, and the VA only records the result in its log
The tenant queues the request for the source's VA cluster and a VA in that cluster picks it up
questions.answer: The tenant queues the request for the source's VA cluster and a VA in that cluster picks it up
questions.explanation: Each source is associated with a VA cluster, and every running VA continually polls that cluster's queue of requests. SailPoint never opens a session into the VA.

questions.stem: Which operating system runs on a SailPoint virtual appliance?
choices: Windows Server Core
Flatcar Container Linux
Ubuntu Server LTS
Red Hat Enterprise Linux
questions.answer: Flatcar Container Linux
questions.explanation: The VA image is built on Flatcar, which is why OS update warnings and Flatcar URLs appear in the VA requirements. Customers do not install the VA software on a general-purpose OS of their choice.

questions.stem: A tenant has two sources built on SaaS connectors, an on-premises Active Directory domain and an on-premises Oracle database. Which of these sources need a VA cluster?
choices: Only the two sources built on SaaS connectors
Only the Oracle database, since Active Directory uses a SaaS connector
All four sources, since every connector runs on a VA
The Active Directory and Oracle database sources
questions.answer: The Active Directory and Oracle database sources
questions.explanation: Systems on the internal network are reached through a VA cluster, while SaaS connectors run in SailPoint's cloud. Active Directory is a classic VA-based connector.

questions.stem: Which VA component performs connector operations such as aggregation, test connection and provisioning against target systems?
choices: The Cloud Connector Gateway (CCG)
The identity profile engine
The network tunnel client
The Privileged Access Gateway
questions.answer: The Cloud Connector Gateway (CCG)
questions.explanation: The Cloud Connector Gateway component, enabled by default on every Identity Security cluster, runs the connectors and writes ccg.log. The Privileged Access Gateway is an optional component for SailPoint Privilege.

questions.stem: Besides aggregation and provisioning, which action on a VA-connected source is also sent as a request to the source's VA cluster?
choices: Changing the owner of the source
Selecting Test Connection on the source
Building a search query on the source's accounts
Editing the source's description
questions.answer: Selecting Test Connection on the source
questions.explanation: Aggregation, test connection, pass-through authentication and provisioning are all queued for the VA cluster because they talk to the target. Descriptions, owners and searches are stored and processed in the tenant.

questions.stem: What is SailPoint's minimum recommendation for the number of VAs in each production cluster?
choices: One VA for every source connected to the cluster, sized to its load
Three VAs, so a majority quorum can vote
Two VAs, so the cluster stays available during rolling updates
One VA, protected by a hypervisor snapshot
questions.answer: Two VAs, so the cluster stays available during rolling updates
questions.explanation: At least two VAs per cluster keep connectivity while SailPoint updates and reboots VAs one at a time. VAs do not use quorum voting, and one VA can serve many sources.

questions.stem: A cluster with a single VA loses connectivity to its sources every time SailPoint applies an update. What should the administrator do?
choices: Place a load balancer in front of the VA
Add a second VA to the cluster
Turn off automatic updates on the cluster
Ask SailPoint to delay updates to a weekend window
questions.answer: Add a second VA to the cluster
questions.explanation: Updates are rolled through a cluster one VA at a time, so a second VA keeps the cluster serving requests. VA updates cannot be skipped or delayed.

questions.stem: An administrator wants a source to always use a particular VA host in the main data center. How are sources and VAs actually associated?
choices: A source is linked to a VA cluster, and any VA in that cluster may process its work
A source is pinned to one VA by its host name
Each VA is dedicated to exactly one source
Sources send their work to every cluster in the tenant, and the fastest cluster answers
questions.answer: A source is linked to a VA cluster, and any VA in that cluster may process its work
questions.explanation: The source's Base Configuration selects a VA cluster, not an individual VA. Whichever VA in the cluster polls the queue first picks up the request.

questions.stem: An organization places VAs from its primary and disaster recovery data centers in one cluster, all running. What happens if the primary data center goes offline?
choices: SailPoint Support must re-pair the DR VAs
Administrators must re-enter the source credentials on a separate DR cluster
The DR VAs keep processing the cluster's requests with no action needed
Each source must be reconnected to the DR data center
questions.answer: The DR VAs keep processing the cluster's requests with no action needed
questions.explanation: With all VAs in one running cluster, the surviving VAs simply keep polling the queue. The trade-off of this strategy is possible latency when a DR VA works with a distant source.

questions.stem: An organization uses separate primary and DR VA clusters and connects all sources to the primary one. What is the main drawback of this switch-clusters strategy?
choices: The DR cluster adds latency to daily provisioning
Both clusters pick up every request, so each change is provisioned twice to every target
The DR VAs stop receiving SailPoint updates
Failover means reconnecting each source to the DR cluster and re-entering its credentials
questions.answer: Failover means reconnecting each source to the DR cluster and re-entering its credentials
questions.explanation: The DR cluster stays updated but idle, so an outage lasts until each source is moved and its credentials re-entered. That is hard when there are many sources.

questions.stem: What does SailPoint require for VAs that serve a sandbox tenant?
choices: Sandbox tenants share the production cluster's VAs
One sandbox VA is enough, because sandbox receives VA updates after production does
Sandbox VAs must sit in the DMZ to keep them isolated
A sandbox cluster with at least two VAs, used to test changes before production
questions.answer: A sandbox cluster with at least two VAs, used to test changes before production
questions.explanation: SailPoint requires at least two VAs per sandbox cluster and similar VA setups in sandbox and production. Sandbox actually receives VA updates about a week before production.

questions.stem: A network architect proposes a load balancer in front of the VAs in a cluster for high availability. What should the administrator advise?
choices: Use a layer 7 load balancer with sticky sessions
Use the load balancer only for provisioning traffic, and leave aggregation direct
It is not required, because VAs in a cluster share work by polling the queue
Use DNS round robin across the VA host names
questions.answer: It is not required, because VAs in a cluster share work by polling the queue
questions.explanation: There is no inbound traffic to balance: each VA pulls requests from its cluster's queue. SailPoint states that a load balancer is not required for HA.

questions.stem: An administrator boots a freshly imported VA image and signs in as the sailpoint user. What should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Change the default password with the passwd command
Run va-bootstrap pair and enter the code in the tenant
Connect the VA cluster to the Active Directory source
Enable debugging on the VA cluster
questions.answer: Change the default password with the passwd command
questions.explanation: SailPoint's procedure is to change the default sailpoint password immediately after the first sign-in. Pairing and connecting sources come after the passphrase is set.

questions.stem: Three VAs are being added to one cluster. What is true about the keyPassphrase set on each of them?
choices: It is generated by the tenant and emailed to the administrator
It must be identical on every VA in the cluster
It is optional once a cluster has two or more VAs
It must be different on each VA in the cluster
questions.answer: It must be identical on every VA in the cluster
questions.explanation: Every VA in a cluster must use the same keyPassphrase so all of them can decrypt the cluster's source credentials. The VA encrypts the passphrase locally after it is set.

questions.stem: After running va-bootstrap pair on a new VA, the administrator has a pairing code. Where is the code entered?
choices: On the cluster's Add New VA page in the Admin UI, within four hours
In the VA's config.yaml before a reboot
In a support case, so SailPoint can pair the VA with the cluster for you
In the source's Base Configuration page
questions.answer: On the cluster's Add New VA page in the Admin UI, within four hours
questions.explanation: The code is entered on the Configure Virtual Appliance page reached from the cluster's Edit view and must be used within four hours. Sources are connected to the cluster only after the VA is connected.

questions.stem: A VA deployed on vSphere must use a fixed address on the server VLAN. How should the administrator set it?
choices: Ask SailPoint Support to assign an address from the tenant
Create the static.network file with the NIC name, address, gateway and DNS, then reboot
Add an ipAddress line to the VA's config.yaml
Enter the address, gateway and DNS on the cluster's Edit page in the Admin UI
questions.answer: Create the static.network file with the NIC name, address, gateway and DNS, then reboot
questions.explanation: Static addressing for local VAs is set in /etc/systemd/network/static.network followed by a reboot. The Admin UI does not manage the VA's network interface.

questions.stem: What is the minimum VA image size SailPoint specifies for a local VA deployment?
choices: 1 processor, 4 GB memory and 40 GB storage
2 processors, 8 GB memory and 64 GB storage
8 processors, 64 GB memory and 1 TB storage
4 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage
questions.answer: 4 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage
questions.explanation: The minimum local VA is 4 CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 128 GB disk, with more added when extra cluster components are enabled. Undersized VAs trigger memory and disk warnings.

questions.stem: A company is placing VAs for its on-premises Active Directory forest. Where should the VAs be deployed?
choices: In a distant cloud region, to isolate them from users
In the DMZ, so they can reach the internet easily
On the internal network, close to the domain controllers
Both on the same VM host, to keep them together
questions.answer: On the internal network, close to the domain controllers
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends VAs near their sources on internal networks, with one VA per VM host for resilience. DMZ placement is not recommended for security, proximity and connectivity reasons.

questions.stem: An administrator paired a new VA a few minutes ago. What shows that the VA has finished its initial configuration?
choices: The connected sources show new account counts
The VA's status changes to Connected
The cluster card shows the Empty Cluster badge
The VA console displays the tenant's URL
questions.answer: The VA's status changes to Connected
questions.explanation: Configuration takes about 30 minutes after pairing, after which the VA status reads Connected. Empty Cluster means the cluster has no VAs at all.

questions.stem: What does each VA hold that lets it decrypt the source credentials it uses to reach target systems?
choices: A shared symmetric key built into every VA image by SailPoint
A copy of every identity's password hash
A 2048-bit RSA private key generated from the key passphrase
The tenant's OAuth client secret
questions.answer: A 2048-bit RSA private key generated from the key passphrase
questions.explanation: Each VA contains an RSA private key derived from the cluster's passphrase and uses it to decrypt credentials. That key is why the VA must sit in a well-protected network zone.

questions.stem: A security architect asks why SailPoint advises against putting VAs in the DMZ. What is the MOST important reason?
choices: SailPoint refuses to pair any VA that has a public IP address on its interface
A VA cannot obtain an IP address inside a DMZ
DMZ firewalls cannot carry outbound HTTPS
The VA holds the key that decrypts source credentials, which a weaker zone exposes
questions.answer: The VA holds the key that decrypts source credentials, which a weaker zone exposes
questions.explanation: Security is the main concern: the VA is a communication backbone holding its private key. Proximity to sources and fewer internal firewall openings are the other reasons.

questions.stem: An administrator has lost the sailpoint user password for a production VA. What is the supported way forward?
choices: Deploy a new VA to replace it
Reset the password from the cluster's Edit page
Pair the VA again to receive a new password
Ask SailPoint Support to reset it remotely
questions.answer: Deploy a new VA to replace it
questions.explanation: SailPoint states that if the sailpoint password is lost, a new VA must be created. The tenant has no way to reset a VA's local password.

questions.stem: An organization fails over by pointing its sources at a different VA cluster. Why must administrators re-enter each source's credentials?
choices: Moving a source deletes its account schema
Credentials expire whenever a VA reboots
Each cluster requires its own separate service account for every source it serves
The stored credentials were encrypted for the original cluster's keys
questions.answer: The stored credentials were encrypted for the original cluster's keys
questions.explanation: Source credentials are encrypted so only the cluster that owns the matching key can decrypt them. A new cluster has its own key, so the credentials must be entered again.

questions.stem: How is traffic between a VA and the SailPoint tenant protected?
choices: The VA starts encrypted HTTPS connections outbound to SailPoint
The tenant opens SSH tunnels to the VA on port 22
SailPoint requires a site-to-site VPN and sends plain traffic inside it
The VA sends signed messages over plain HTTP on port 80
questions.answer: The VA starts encrypted HTTPS connections outbound to SailPoint
questions.explanation: VA communication uses TLS-protected HTTPS on port 443 that the VA initiates. A network tunnel option exists, but no VPN or inbound SSH from SailPoint is required.

questions.stem: A hardening review asks which inbound port on the VAs should be restricted to internal administrator networks. Which port is it?
choices: Port 53 for DNS
Port 123 for NTP
Port 22 for SSH
Port 443 for HTTPS
questions.answer: Port 22 for SSH
questions.explanation: SSH on 22 is the only inbound port in the VA requirements and is used by administrators to sign in. Ports 443, 53 and 123 are outbound.

questions.stem: A Source Admin wants one page that shows the health of every VA cluster in the tenant. Where should the admin go?
choices: Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
Admin > Connections > Sources > Accounts
Search > Events filtered on the cluster name
questions.answer: Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
questions.explanation: The Virtual Appliances page shows a card for each cluster with status and alert badges. The Sources pages show source status, not VA health.

questions.stem: The operations team wants an email whenever a VA goes down or a cluster reports a health warning. What should the administrator configure?
choices: Organization health notifications for VA and cluster problems
A scheduled search on the cluster's sources
Enable Debugging on each cluster
A subscription to the Provisioning Activity report
questions.answer: Organization health notifications for VA and cluster problems
questions.explanation: ISC can send notification emails when a VA goes down or a cluster has a health warning or error. Debug logging only increases log detail.

questions.stem: A cluster card shows a warning badge. How can the administrator find which VA has the problem and see its details?
choices: Download ccg.log from the source's configuration page and search for the VA
Follow the health badge to the VA list and select the affected VA
Run Test Connection on every source in the cluster
Open the identity profile and run a preview
questions.answer: Follow the health badge to the VA list and select the affected VA
questions.explanation: The health badge links to the cluster's VA list, where each VA shows timestamp, category, severity and the error message. Test Connection checks a source, not the VA's health record.

questions.stem: Before restarting a cluster, an administrator wants to check whether the processes on a VA are busy. Where is this shown?
choices: The cluster's Time Zone setting on the Edit page
The Admin Dashboard Tasks list
The VA's VA Components tab, which lists each process as OK, Busy or Error
The source's Accounts tab, which lists the aggregations running on each VA
questions.answer: The VA's VA Components tab, which lists each process as OK, Busy or Error
questions.explanation: The VA Components view reports each process status so admins can see whether it is available for work or updates. Busy processes may be running long jobs such as aggregations.

questions.stem: Which part of the Admin Dashboard gives a quick view of VA cluster health?
choices: The Certifications tile in the campaigns panel
The Tasks list in the work panel
The Identities tile in the overview panel
The Clusters tile in the system components status panel
questions.answer: The Clusters tile in the system components status panel
questions.explanation: The system components status panel includes a Clusters tile that summarizes cluster health. The other tiles cover identities, work and campaigns.

questions.stem: An administrator must list every source that depends on a VA cluster before planned maintenance. Where is that list?
choices: In the cluster's Cluster Components page
In Search, under Account Activity
On the cluster's Details page, Connections tab
In each VA's local log folder
questions.answer: On the cluster's Details page, Connections tab
questions.explanation: The Connections tab of the cluster Details page lists all connected sources with their status. Cluster Components only lists optional product components.

questions.stem: A cluster card shows the badge Only 1 VA in Cluster. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Turn on debugging on the remaining VA
Add at least one more VA to the cluster
Delete the cluster and create a new one
Restart the cluster to clear the badge
questions.answer: Add at least one more VA to the cluster
questions.explanation: The badge warns that the cluster has no redundancy for updates or outages. A restart does not change the VA count.

questions.stem: A newly created cluster shows the Empty Cluster badge. What does this mean?
choices: The cluster has no VAs and cannot be used until some are added
All of the cluster's VAs are inactive
The cluster's logs have been cleared
The cluster has VAs but no sources have been connected to it yet
questions.answer: The cluster has no VAs and cannot be used until some are added
questions.explanation: Empty Cluster means no VAs exist in it. A cluster with VAs but no sources does not show this badge, and inactive VAs produce a different badge.

questions.stem: A two-VA cluster shows VA Update in Progress during business hours. What is the expected impact on its sources?
choices: The sources fall back to SaaS connectors
All source connections stop until the update ends on every VA in the cluster
Provisioning is queued but aggregation stops
Normal cluster operation continues while one VA is being configured
questions.answer: Normal cluster operation continues while one VA is being configured
questions.explanation: With two or more VAs, one keeps working while the other updates. Only a single-VA cluster loses service during updates.

questions.stem: One VA in a cluster shows Inactive State. What does SailPoint suggest as the next step?
choices: Change the cluster's time zone
Work with the network administrator, because the VA cannot connect
Re-enter the service account credentials on each source connected to the cluster
Delete the cluster and every source on it
questions.answer: Work with the network administrator, because the VA cannot connect
questions.explanation: Inactive State means the VA cannot connect, which usually points to network issues. Credentials and time zones are unrelated to the VA's own connection.

questions.stem: Which VA status means the VA is operating as expected?
choices: Connected
Inactive State
Update in Progress
Configuration Incomplete
questions.answer: Connected
questions.explanation: Connected is the healthy steady state of a VA. Configuration Incomplete means pairing failed, and Update in Progress is a temporary state.

questions.stem: A cluster card shows All VAs Inactive. What is the MOST likely impact on its sources?
choices: Sources keep working, because the tenant connects to their targets directly instead
Provisioning switches to manual tasks automatically
Aggregation, test connection and provisioning for those sources cannot run
Only scheduled aggregations are delayed
questions.answer: Aggregation, test connection and provisioning for those sources cannot run
questions.explanation: If no VA in the cluster can connect, nothing pulls the cluster's requests, so all source operations stall. The tenant has no direct path to VA-based sources.

questions.stem: An administrator is adding a new VA to an existing standard cluster. Put the steps in order.
items: Select Edit on the cluster, then Virtual Appliances > Add New > VA
Start the VA image and sign in as the sailpoint user
Change the default sailpoint password with passwd
Run va-bootstrap set-passphrase with the cluster's keyPassphrase
Run va-bootstrap pair and enter the code in the Admin UI
Wait for the VA status to change to Connected
questions.explanation: The VA is created in the cluster, then the image is started and secured, the passphrase is set and the VA is paired. Configuration finishes about 30 minutes later when the status reads Connected.

questions.stem: Match each VA or cluster badge to what it means.

pairs.match: The cluster has no VAs and cannot be used
The cluster has no redundancy for updates
An update failed to apply and a cluster restart is needed
The VA cannot connect and the network should be checked
The VA is operating as expected

targets_extra: The source's service account password has expired
questions.explanation: Cluster badges describe VA count and update state, while VA badges describe each VA's connection. Expired source credentials show on the source, not as a VA badge.

questions.stem: A firewall team is writing rules for new VAs. Which TWO outbound connections do the VAs need in a standard configuration?
choices: HTTPS on port 443 to the required SailPoint and AWS URLs
DNS on port 53 to name servers
Inbound SSH on port 22 from SailPoint's cloud
LDAP on port 389 from SailPoint's cloud to the VA
SMTP on port 25 to send notification emails
answers: HTTPS on port 443 to the required SailPoint and AWS URLs
DNS on port 53 to name servers
questions.explanation: VAs need outbound 443 and DNS on 53, plus NTP on 123 unless a local NTP server is used. SailPoint never connects inbound to the VA, and notification email is sent by the tenant.

questions.stem: A cluster reports a Network Error saying it cannot reach required endpoints. What should the administrator check FIRST?
choices: That the cluster's time zone matches the sources
That the source service account password is current and has not been locked out
That inbound 443 is open from the tenant to each VA
That the firewall allows outbound HTTPS to the required SailPoint and AWS URLs
questions.answer: That the firewall allows outbound HTTPS to the required SailPoint and AWS URLs
questions.explanation: The Network Error points to blocked outbound traffic to the URLs in the VA requirements. Source credentials affect target connections, not the VA's reach to SailPoint.

questions.stem: The corporate firewall can only allow outbound traffic by IP address, not by domain name. Which VA configuration is designed for this?
choices: Hosting the VA in the DMZ
The network tunnel VA configuration
Allowing the current IP addresses of the AWS endpoints
The standard VA configuration
questions.answer: The network tunnel VA configuration
questions.explanation: SailPoint suggests a network tunnel configuration when firewalls do not support domain entries, because it uses fixed regional addresses. Allowing service endpoint IPs is not supported.

questions.stem: A tenant runs in the Frankfurt AWS region. Which SQS endpoints must the VAs be allowed to reach?
choices: Any regional SQS endpoint, because the VA chooses the nearest one automatically
Only sqs.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com
Only sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Both sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and sqs.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com
questions.answer: Both sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and sqs.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com
questions.explanation: SailPoint requires the us-east-1 URL for each AWS service plus the region-specific one when the tenant is elsewhere. Allowing only the local region breaks part of the VA's communication.

questions.stem: After the security team turns on TLS inspection, new VAs fail to connect to the tenant. What should the administrator do?
choices: Configure the VAs to trust the private root CA the inspection device uses
Turn off certificate validation on the VAs
Allow the VAs by IP address instead of URL
Move the VAs into the DMZ so their traffic bypasses the inspection device
questions.answer: Configure the VAs to trust the private root CA the inspection device uses
questions.explanation: VAs reject untrusted certificates, so the inspection CA must be trusted on the VA. Disabling validation is not supported and would weaken security.

questions.stem: A source shows Target system failing while its VA cluster is healthy. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VA cannot reach SailPoint's AWS endpoints, so the cluster's queue is not polled
The source has no Create Account policy
The VA cannot reach the target or the source's service credentials are no longer valid
The cluster has only one VA
questions.answer: The VA cannot reach the target or the source's service credentials are no longer valid
questions.explanation: This banner means the VA works but the target is unreachable, for example expired service credentials, a changed host name or a network route issue. A VA connectivity issue would show on the cluster instead.

questions.stem: A healthy VA cannot reach a database server whose address is 10.255.255.245, while other servers work. What explains this?
choices: The VA needs a second network card for databases
The address is in a range SailPoint reserves, so VA traffic to it does not route
The database requires an inbound connection from SailPoint's cloud on its listener port
JDBC sources must use a SaaS connector
questions.answer: The address is in a range SailPoint reserves, so VA traffic to it does not route
questions.explanation: SailPoint reserves 10.255.255.241/28 internally, so sources in that range cannot be reached from any VA configuration. Readdressing the server is the fix.

questions.stem: Security wants to block outbound port 123. What must the administrator do before closing it?
choices: Disable time synchronization on the VAs
Set the cluster time zone to UTC in the Admin UI
Point every VA at an internal NTP server in timesyncd.conf and restart the time service
Point only the first VA in each cluster at an internal NTP server; the others copy its time
questions.answer: Point every VA at an internal NTP server in timesyncd.conf and restart the time service
questions.explanation: Each VA must be configured individually to use internal NTP, and port 123 can close only after all of them are. Accurate time is required for the VA to work.

questions.stem: After changing NTP servers on a VA, which command confirms the VA's time synchronization status?
choices: sudo update_engine_client -status
passwd
va-bootstrap pair
timedatectl status
questions.answer: timedatectl status
questions.explanation: timedatectl status shows the system clock and whether it is synchronized. The update engine client reports Flatcar OS update state, not time.

questions.stem: A new VA connects to the tenant but cannot resolve the host names of internal domain controllers. What should the administrator check?
choices: The DNS entry in the VA's static.network file points to internal DNS servers
The keyPassphrase on this VA matches the one set on the other VAs in the cluster
The cluster time zone is the same as the domain's
Port 22 is open from the domain controllers
questions.answer: The DNS entry in the VA's static.network file points to internal DNS servers
questions.explanation: VAs must use internal DNS to find on-premises sources, set with the DNS line in static.network. The passphrase and time zone do not affect name resolution.

questions.stem: Company policy forces all outbound web traffic through an HTTP proxy. Which VA configuration should the administrator use?
choices: The network tunnel configuration in the DMZ
The standard configuration with a load balancer
The HTTP proxy VA configuration
A VA with no outbound access at all
questions.answer: The HTTP proxy VA configuration
questions.explanation: ISC supports standard, HTTP proxy and network tunnel VA configurations, and the proxy option is designed for proxied outbound traffic. Some cluster components support only standard VAs.

questions.stem: VAs running on Hyper-V show irregular routing and DNS problems. Which change does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Move the VA to Generation 2 hardware
Mask the waagent service and reboot the VA
Add a second network adapter for DNS
Enable debugging on the cluster
questions.answer: Mask the waagent service and reboot the VA
questions.explanation: Hyper-V images ship with the Azure waagent enabled, which can disrupt DNS and routing; masking it fixes this. Debug logging would only record the symptoms.

questions.stem: Aggregations from a VA fail with errors that suggest token and certificate times are invalid. Which check is MOST relevant?
choices: Whether the VA's clock is synchronized with an NTP server
Whether the source has a Create Account policy
Whether the VA has enough disk space for logs
Whether the cluster has the Privileged Access Gateway enabled
questions.answer: Whether the VA's clock is synchronized with an NTP server
questions.explanation: Clock drift makes time-based security checks fail, which is why VAs must reach an NTP server. Disk and provisioning settings do not affect time validation.

questions.stem: Where on a VA does the administrator find the Cloud Connector Gateway log that records connector activity?
choices: config.yaml in /home/sailpoint
static.network in /etc/systemd/network
timesyncd.conf in /etc/systemd
ccg.log in /home/sailpoint/log
questions.answer: ccg.log in /home/sailpoint/log
questions.explanation: Connector operations are logged in ccg.log under /home/sailpoint/log. The other files hold VA configuration, networking and time settings.

questions.stem: An administrator selects Enable Debugging on a VA cluster. What does this do?
choices: Turns on debug logging for one source until it is turned off
Raises only the Active Directory connector to TRACE
Turns on debug-level logging for all VAs in the cluster for 24 hours
Sends the VA logs to SailPoint Support every hour
questions.answer: Turns on debug-level logging for all VAs in the cluster for 24 hours
questions.explanation: Enable Debugging gives 24 hours of verbose logging on every VA in the cluster. Connector-specific levels are set through the cluster's log configuration instead.

questions.stem: How large can a VA log file grow before it is replaced when debugging is NOT enabled?
choices: 512 MB
2 GB
Unlimited, until the disk fills
64 MB
questions.answer: 512 MB
questions.explanation: Without debugging, log files are replaced once they reach 512 MB. With debugging, all log data for 24 hours is kept regardless of size.

questions.stem: A test connection on a VA-based source fails with a generic message in the Admin UI. What is the BEST next step?
choices: Restart the VA cluster immediately
Review ccg.log around the failure time for the error and exception details
Raise the source's account deletion threshold and run the test connection again
Delete and recreate the source
questions.answer: Review ccg.log around the failure time for the error and exception details
questions.explanation: The VA log shows the inner error, such as an LDAP code or exception, that the UI summarizes. Recreating or restarting without evidence risks downtime.

questions.stem: While reading connector logs after a failure, which search approach does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Search for the generic message shown in the UI
Search only for INFO lines that mention the tenant name and the source name
Search the newest line in the file only
Search near the failure time for ERROR, Exception and HTTP or LDAP codes
questions.answer: Search near the failure time for ERROR, Exception and HTTP or LDAP codes
questions.explanation: The useful clues are error lines, exceptions and protocol codes near the failure time. Keywords from the inner message, not the generic UI text, lead to the right resolution.

questions.stem: An admin turned on Enable Debugging last week and forgot about it. A month later the cluster shows a Disk Warning. What is the MOST likely link?
choices: Debug mode disables log rotation forever
Debugging stores account data on the VA disk
Debugging encrypts each log file, which doubles its size on the VA's disk over time
Verbose logs filled the disk while debugging stayed on or was turned on again
questions.answer: Verbose logs filled the disk while debugging stayed on or was turned on again
questions.explanation: SailPoint's first recommendation for a Disk Warning is to check log levels and turn off debug logging that is not needed, since verbose logs use the most space. Debug mode does not store identity data.

questions.stem: A cluster card shows VA Did Not Update. What should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Restart the cluster from the card's menu
Delete the VA and pair it again
Open a support case before taking any action
Disconnect every source from the cluster
questions.answer: Restart the cluster from the card's menu
questions.explanation: SailPoint's guidance for VA Did Not Update is to restart the cluster, then contact Support if the problem persists. Deleting VAs is a last resort.

questions.stem: One of three VAs in a cluster has been disconnected for weeks. Why does this matter for the other two?
choices: SailPoint deletes the cluster after seven days
The other two VAs must be paired again
No software or maintenance updates are applied to any VA in that cluster
The other two VAs stop processing requests until the third VA comes back online
questions.answer: No software or maintenance updates are applied to any VA in that cluster
questions.explanation: If any VA in a cluster is not connected, SailPoint does not update any VA in it. Fixing or removing the disconnected VA lets updates resume.

questions.stem: A change board asks to postpone next week's VA update until after quarter end. What should the administrator explain?
choices: Updates can be blocked by removing port 443 for that week
VA updates cannot be skipped or delayed, but sandbox usually gets them about a week earlier
Updates only apply when an admin approves them
Updates can be postponed for up to 30 days from the cluster's Edit page in the Admin UI
questions.answer: VA updates cannot be skipped or delayed, but sandbox usually gets them about a week earlier
questions.explanation: SailPoint manages updates and does not allow delays, so sandbox clusters act as an early check. Blocking traffic would break the VA, not postpone the update.

questions.stem: A cluster shows an OS Update Warning saying the Flatcar update requires a reboot. What resolves it?
choices: Set the cluster time zone again
Confirm the pending update with the update engine client and reboot the VA
Re-enter the cluster's keyPassphrase
Reinstall the VA from the latest image and pair it with the cluster again
questions.answer: Confirm the pending update with the update engine client and reboot the VA
questions.explanation: The warning means Flatcar downloaded an update that needs a reboot to finish. Rebuilding the VA is unnecessary.

questions.stem: A cluster shows a Service Stability Warning because a container restarted more than 10 times in 30 minutes. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Increase the account deletion threshold
Turn off the Cloud Connector Gateway component until the restarts stop
Check that VA services are up to date and restart the cluster
Move the sources to a SaaS connector
questions.answer: Check that VA services are up to date and restart the cluster
questions.explanation: Repeated container restarts point to an unhealthy or out-of-date service, and a cluster restart is the documented fix. Disabling the CCG would stop all connector work.

questions.stem: A long account aggregation stopped midway during a VA rolling update. What is the BEST response?
choices: Run the aggregation again after the update, since long jobs can be interrupted
Ask SailPoint to roll back the update
Raise the aggregation's log level to TRACE permanently so the next interruption is logged
Delete the VA that was updated
questions.answer: Run the aggregation again after the update, since long jobs can be interrupted
questions.explanation: SailPoint warns that in-progress processes, such as long aggregations, may be interrupted during updates even though cluster availability is kept. Rerunning the job is the normal recovery.

questions.stem: What condition triggers a VA Disk Warning?
choices: Any log file larger than 10 MB
File system usage over 99 %
File system usage over 50 %
File system usage over 80 %
questions.answer: File system usage over 80 %
questions.explanation: A Disk Warning appears above 80 % usage and a Disk Error above 90 %. SailPoint advises checking log levels and turning off unneeded debug logging.

questions.stem: A VA reports a Disk Error. What does that mean?
choices: The VA cannot read its configuration file
The log folder was deleted
A disk on the hypervisor has failed
Storage usage is over 90 % and the disk is effectively full
questions.answer: Storage usage is over 90 % and the disk is effectively full
questions.explanation: Disk Error means usage above 90 %. The fixes are the same as for the warning: reduce verbose logging and clear or split logs.

questions.stem: A VA shows a Memory Warning. What is the condition behind it?
choices: A single process used memory for longer than one hour
Memory use briefly reached 50 % during an aggregation
Average memory use over the last 12 hours is above 80 %
The VA has more than 16 GB of memory
questions.answer: Average memory use over the last 12 hours is above 80 %
questions.explanation: Memory warnings are based on the 12-hour average, above 80 % for a warning and 90 % for an error. The fix is to give the VA enough memory for its workload.

questions.stem: VAs deployed on small cloud instances keep showing Memory Error. What should the administrator do?
choices: Resize the instances to meet SailPoint's minimum VA sizes
Remove the second VA from the cluster to free memory for the first one
Turn on debugging to find the leak
Lower the root log level to ERROR
questions.answer: Resize the instances to meet SailPoint's minimum VA sizes
questions.explanation: Persistent memory errors mean the VA is undersized; SailPoint publishes minimum sizes such as M5.xlarge-class instances. Removing a VA would remove redundancy and add load.

questions.stem: An administrator enables the Privileged Access Gateway component on an existing cluster. What must also happen?
choices: The cluster must be converted to a different cluster type that supports the component
Each VA must get extra processors and memory on top of the minimum size
Each VA must be paired again
Sources must be moved to a new cluster
questions.answer: Each VA must get extra processors and memory on top of the minimum size
questions.explanation: Each enabled component raises the per-VA resource minimum, and the administrator is responsible for adding those resources. The cluster type itself cannot be changed.

questions.stem: A cluster shows a Certificate Expiration Warning. What should the administrator do?
choices: Change the keyPassphrase on every VA
Re-pair each VA to get a new key pair
Restart the cluster so each VA requests a new certificate from SailPoint automatically
Renew the certificate in /home/sailpoint/ca-certificates and remove the expired one
questions.answer: Renew the certificate in /home/sailpoint/ca-certificates and remove the expired one
questions.explanation: The warning fires when a certificate in the VA's certificate folder has expired or expires within 30 days. Restarting or re-pairing does not renew it.

questions.stem: A VA must move to new hypervisor hardware. What is SailPoint's recommended approach?
choices: Export the VA's config.yaml and import it on a new VM
Create a new VA, confirm it connects, then delete the old one
Live-migrate the VA with the hypervisor's tools
Copy the VA's disk to the new host and boot it
questions.answer: Create a new VA, confirm it connects, then delete the old one
questions.explanation: SailPoint strongly advises against moving or migrating VAs. Building a new VA and removing the old one keeps the cluster healthy.

questions.stem: An administrator deletes a VA from a cluster in the Admin UI. What else must be done?
choices: Delete the cluster as well
Re-enter the service account credentials on every source connected to the cluster
Shut down the related VA instance on the virtualization platform
Restart the tenant
questions.answer: Shut down the related VA instance on the virtualization platform
questions.explanation: Leaving the deleted VA's VM running can degrade performance or cause downtime. Source credentials remain valid because the cluster is unchanged.

questions.stem: The Admin UI will not let an administrator delete a VA. It is the only VA in its cluster. What is the likely reason?
choices: A source is still attached to the cluster
Debugging is enabled on the cluster
The VA is in the Connected state
The cluster time zone is not set
questions.answer: A source is still attached to the cluster
questions.explanation: A single VA cannot be deleted while its cluster still serves a source; the source must first be reassigned to another cluster. Connection state and debugging do not block deletion.

questions.stem: How does an administrator disconnect a VA cluster from a source?
choices: Delete the source's account schema
Turn off the Cloud Connector Gateway on the cluster
Select a different VA cluster in the source's Base Configuration and save
Remove the source from the list on the cluster's Connections tab and save the change
questions.answer: Select a different VA cluster in the source's Base Configuration and save
questions.explanation: The cluster is chosen on the source, so disconnecting means choosing another cluster there. The Connections tab only lists sources.

questions.stem: A production VA cluster has failed beyond repair. What should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Re-enter credentials on the sources while still on the failed cluster
Create a new cluster with at least two VAs
Delete the failed cluster
Restart the tenant from the Admin Dashboard
questions.answer: Create a new cluster with at least two VAs
questions.explanation: Recovery starts by building the replacement cluster, then noting and reconnecting the sources, verifying connections and only then deleting the failed cluster. Deleting first loses the record of connected sources.

questions.stem: After moving all sources to a replacement cluster, how should the administrator confirm the move before deleting the failed cluster?
choices: Check the new cluster's Connections tab lists the same sources
Check the Identities list for new identities
Check that each failed VA shows a new pairing code on the cluster's Edit page
Check the failed cluster still shows Connected
questions.answer: Check the new cluster's Connections tab lists the same sources
questions.explanation: The Connections tab on the new cluster's Details page shows every source attached to it. Matching it against the failed cluster's list confirms no source was missed.

questions.stem: A production VA cluster has failed. Put the recovery steps in order.
items: Create a new cluster with at least two VAs
Note the sources on the failed cluster's Connections tab
Select the new cluster in each source's Base Configuration
Confirm the new cluster's Connections tab lists the same sources
questions.explanation: The replacement is built first, the source list is captured, each source is moved and checked, and only then is the failed cluster removed. Deleting earlier would lose the record of which sources to move.

questions.stem: Match each VA cluster warning to the recommended response.

pairs.match: Turn off debug logging that is not needed
Give the VAs enough memory for SailPoint's sizing
Allow VA traffic to the required URLs
Renew the certificate in the VA's certificate folder
Reboot the VA to finish the Flatcar update

targets_extra: Raise the source's account deletion threshold
questions.explanation: Each warning maps to the documented fix: logging for disk, sizing for memory, firewall rules for network, certificates and reboots. The deletion threshold belongs to aggregation, not VA health.

questions.stem: Security will close outbound port 123 for all VAs. Which TWO steps must be done on each VA first?
choices: Add internal servers to the NTP line in timesyncd.conf
Restart the systemd-timesyncd service
Set the cluster time zone to UTC in the Admin UI
Run va-bootstrap pair again
Enable Debugging on the cluster
answers: Add internal servers to the NTP line in timesyncd.conf
questions.explanation: Each VA is pointed at local NTP servers in /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf and the time service restarted, then checked with timedatectl status. The cluster time zone only sets aggregation schedule offsets.
